backlog.title: Commit Generation & Agent Tool Safety
backlog.description: Implement §9.10 (new) consolidating commit-message generation (stagecoach binary delegation), commit-identity structural guard (self-source-scan), snapshot-based atomic plumbing commit (§5.1 new blocks), ARG_MAX-safe staging, baseline .gitignore scaffolding, per-role agent tool matrix, and bash remote-mutation denylist. Also covers §9.1 tech-stack bullet, §4.1 .gitignore cross-reference, and terminology cleanup (stagecoach-the-in-process-tool → Smart Commit).

milestones.title: Snapshot-Based Atomic Smart Commit + ARG_MAX-safe staging + baseline .gitignore scaffolding
milestones.description: Rewrite smartCommit to use git plumbing (write-tree → commit-tree → CAS update-ref) for atomicity and identity transparency. Refactor staging to be ARG_MAX-safe (pathspec default, chunked filtered sets). Add .gitignore scaffolding mandate to the breakdown prompt. Per §5.1 new blocks.

tasks.title: Git plumbing primitives: write-tree, commit-tree, CAS update-ref
tasks.description: Create three new git-plumbing functions as argv-vector execs (never sh -c) to support the snapshot-based atomic commit. These live in src/tools/git-mcp.ts alongside the existing simple-git wrappers, using simpleGit.raw() or direct child_process.execFile.

subtasks.title: gitWriteTree — freeze index into immutable tree object
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Architecture findings in plan/015_459c7d9be558/architecture/system_context.md §2.2 and §3.2. git-mcp.ts currently uses simple-git exclusively — no raw plumbing exists. simpleGit.raw(['write-tree']) uses child_process.execFile internally (NOT shell), satisfying §5.1 'never sh -c'. The function gitStatus at line ~336 shows the validateRepositoryPath + simpleGit pattern to follow.
2. INPUT: A repo path string (validated via the existing validateRepositoryPath helper at line ~202 of git-mcp.ts). No other inputs — write-tree operates on the current index.
3. LOGIC: Implement gitWriteTree(repoPath?) that runs `git write-tree` via simpleGit.raw(['write-tree']). Returns { success: true, treeSha: string }. On non-zero exit (unresolved merge conflicts — write-tree fails when the index has conflict markers), return { success: false, error: 'Cannot write-tree: unresolved merge conflicts in the index — resolve them first' }. Export the function and a result type GitWriteTreeResult from git-mcp.ts. Build as an argv vector — never interpolate into a shell string.
4. OUTPUT: Exported async function gitWriteTree(repoPath?) → GitWriteTreeResult from src/tools/git-mcp.ts. Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S1 (smartCommit rewrite).
5. DOCS: JSDoc on gitWriteTree citing §5.1 'git write-tree — freeze the current index into an immutable tree object (TREE_SHA)'.

subtasks.title: gitCommitTree — create dangling commit from tree + parent + message
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per system_context.md §3.2, simpleGit.raw() uses execFile (argv, not shell). The message for commit-tree travels via the -m flag for short messages. For messages with embedded newlines (multi-line commit bodies), pass via stdin or use multiple -m flags (git concatenates). §5.1: 'The diff payload fed to message generation MUST travel via stdin, never interpolated into an argument.'
2. INPUT: { treeSha: string; message: string; parentSha?: string; repoPath?: string }. parentSha is OPTIONAL — omitted for rootless repos (first commit). From P1.M1.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Implement gitCommitTree that builds the argv vector: ['commit-tree', treeSha, '-m', message] and optionally prepends ['-p', parentSha] when parentSha is provided. Run via simpleGit.raw() or direct execFile. The message MUST NOT be interpolated into a shell string — pass as an argv element or via stdin (git commit-tree reads -m arg directly). Returns { success: true, commitSha: string }. On failure, returns { success: false, error: string }.
4. OUTPUT: Exported async function gitCommitTree(input) → GitCommitTreeResult from src/tools/git-mcp.ts. Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S2.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on gitCommitTree citing §5.1 step 2 'git commit-tree (-p <parent>) -m <msg> <tree> — create a commit object from TREE_SHA, PARENT_SHA, and the message. This touches no ref; the commit is dangling until update-ref.'

subtasks.title: gitUpdateRefCAS — atomic compare-and-swap HEAD advance
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Per system_context.md §2.2 and §5.2, the CAS form `git update-ref HEAD <new> <expected-old>` atomically advances HEAD only if its current value equals expected-old. simpleGit.raw() uses execFile internally. Rootless repos: omit the expected-old argument entirely (first commit has no old HEAD to compare).
2. INPUT: { newSha: string; expectedOldSha?: string; repoPath?: string }. expectedOldSha is OPTIONAL — omitted for rootless repos. From P1.M1.T3.S1 (PARENT_SHA) and P1.M1.T1.S2 (new commit SHA).
3. LOGIC: Implement gitUpdateRefCAS that builds argv: ['update-ref', 'HEAD', newSha] and appends expectedOldSha when provided. Run via simpleGit.raw(). On success → { success: true }. On CAS failure (HEAD moved during generation — git exits non-zero with 'ref is at <actual> but expected <expected>') → { success: false, error: string, casFailure: true }. NEVER force the update.
4. OUTPUT: Exported async function gitUpdateRefCAS(input) → GitUpdateRefCASResult from src/tools/git-mcp.ts. Consumed by P1.M1.T3.S2.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on gitUpdateRefCAS citing §5.1 step 3 'CAS (compare-and-swap) form atomically advances HEAD only if its current value still equals PARENT_SHA. If HEAD moved (concurrent commit), the update refuses.'

tasks.title: ARG_MAX-safe staging refactor
tasks.description: Refactor the staging path in git-commit.ts/smartCommit so it no longer enumerates every file path into an explicit argv (which overflows ARG_MAX on repos with unignored node_modules/). Default to pathspec staging (git add -A); chunk filtered sets under an ARG_MAX byte budget.

subtasks.title: Pathspec-default staging + ARG_MAX chunked filtered sets
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: system_context.md §2.1 — current smartCommit calls gitAdd(repoRoot, filteredFiles) which calls git.add(['--', ...everyFile]) via simple-git. A repo with unignored node_modules/ (tens of thousands of files) overflows kernel ARG_MAX → spawn E2BIG → silently strands task status. git-mcp.ts gitAdd (line ~432) already supports `files ?? ['.']` → `git.add('.')` for the all-files path. The fix: stage by pathspec by default, chunk explicit filtered sets.
2. INPUT: The current smartCommit flow provides a `filteredFiles: string[]` (files minus PROTECTED_FILES). The gitAdd function in git-mcp.ts accepts { path, files? }.
3. LOGIC: In smartCommit (src/utils/git-commit.ts), change the staging strategy: (a) When no protected files were filtered OUT (common case), stage with pathspec `git add -A` (or gitAdd with files undefined → `git.add('.')`) — this respects .gitignore and never overflows ARG_MAX. (b) When protected files WERE filtered out, stage all files with `git add -A` first, then UNSTAGE the protected files via git reset HEAD -- <protectedfile> (the existing gitUnstagePath function already does this). This avoids ever building a massive explicit path list. If an explicit filtered set is unavoidable, chunk the path list into batches under an ARG_MAX byte budget (estimate ~128KB per exec on Linux; batch so total argv bytes stay well under). Keep restore_critical_files() running AFTER staging (unchanged). The existing gitAdd function already handles `files = ['.']` → `git.add('.')`, so modify smartCommit to pass `files: ['.']` or undefined for the default path, and use unstage for protected files.
4. OUTPUT: Modified staging logic in smartCommit (src/utils/git-commit.ts) that never passes a massive explicit file list to gitAdd. No new exported interface (internal refactor). smartCommit's signature and return type are unchanged.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on the staging section of smartCommit citing §5.1 'ARG_MAX-safe staging (no argument-vector overflow) — stage by pathspec (git add -A / git add .), and where an explicit filtered set is needed, chunk the path list into batches under an ARG_MAX byte budget.'

tasks.title: Rewrite smartCommit to snapshot-based atomic plumbing commit
tasks.description: Integrate the new plumbing primitives (T1) into smartCommit so the commit is atomic (write-tree → commit-tree → CAS update-ref), identity-transparent (no user.name/user.email/GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* injection), and handles all §5.1 edge cases (rootless repo, merge conflicts, HEAD-moved-during-generation, timeout/SIGINT rescue).

subtasks.title: Pre-generation: capture PARENT_SHA, write-tree snapshot, identity transparency
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: system_context.md §2.1 — current smartCommit flow is gitStatus → gitAdd → restore_critical_files → gitDiff(staged) → generateCommitMessage → formatCommitMessage → gitCommit. The plumbing rewrite inserts BEFORE message generation: capture PARENT_SHA, run write-tree. PARENT_SHA is `git rev-parse HEAD` (or empty for rootless). Note: this subtask focuses on the pre-generation snapshot; message generation delegation is P1.M2.T2.
2. INPUT: The new plumbing functions from P1.M1.T1.S1 (gitWriteTree), P1.M1.T1.S2 (gitCommitTree), P1.M1.T1.S3 (gitUpdateRefCAS). The ARG_MAX-safe staging from P1.M1.T2.S1.
3. LOGIC: In smartCommit (src/utils/git-commit.ts), after staging + restore_critical_files: (a) Capture PARENT_SHA via `git rev-parse HEAD` — detect rootless repo (no commits → HEAD unborn → rev-parse fails → parentSha = undefined). (b) Call gitWriteTree(repoRoot) → if success=false, abort BEFORE any message generation with the merge-conflict error (return null or throw per smartCommit's never-fail contract — log and return null). (c) Capture TREE_SHA. NEVER set user.name/user.email or pass GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env vars on any git subprocess in this path — the plumbing functions inherit the repo's existing git config only. (d) Proceed to message generation (existing path, which P1.M2.T2 will rewire to stagecoach). The PARENT_SHA and TREE_SHA are captured here and consumed by P1.M1.T3.S2.
4. OUTPUT: Modified smartCommit in src/utils/git-commit.ts that captures PARENT_SHA + TREE_SHA before message generation. No new exports — internal integration. The PARENT_SHA/TREE_SHA values flow to P1.M1.T3.S2.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on smartCommit updated to cite §5.1 'Snapshot-Based Atomic Single-Commit' + 'Commit-identity transparency — the subsystem MUST NOT set, override, or inject any git author/committer identity.'

subtasks.title: Post-generation: commit-tree + CAS update-ref, edge-case handling
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: system_context.md §2.1 — the current smartCommit ends with gitCommit(repoRoot, formattedMessage) using simple-git's git.commit(). This must be replaced with: commit-tree (dangling commit) → CAS update-ref. The existing COMMIT_RETRY_MAX retry/fallback layer wraps generateCommitMessage — on fallback, use the PLUMBING commit with the placeholder message (not simple-git's git.commit()). The formatCommitMessage function layers the task-prefix and is unchanged.
2. INPUT: PARENT_SHA and TREE_SHA from P1.M1.T3.S1. formattedMessage from formatCommitMessage (existing). gitCommitTree from P1.M1.T1.S2. gitUpdateRefCAS from P1.M1.T1.S3.
3. LOGIC: After message resolution (generateCommitMessage or fallback): (a) Call gitCommitTree({ treeSha, message: formattedMessage, parentSha }) → newSha. (b) Call gitUpdateRefCAS({ newSha, expectedOldSha: parentSha }) — rootless: omit expectedOldSha. (c) On CAS success → return newSha (commit hash). (d) On CAS FAILURE (HEAD moved during generation — casFailure: true) → MUST NOT force. Surface the generated message + manual recovery recipe: log the message, the TREE_SHA, PARENT_SHA, newSha, and the command `git commit-tree -p <PARENT_SHA> -m "<msg>" <TREE_SHA> | xargs git update-ref HEAD`. Exit non-zero (throw or return a special error — smartCommit's never-fail contract may need a narrow exception here since this is a safety-critical CAS refusal). (e) The retry/fallback layer remains: on generateCommitMessage failure after COMMIT_RETRY_MAX retries, buildFallbackCommitMessage produces a placeholder, and the plumbing commit runs with that placeholder (same atomic path).
4. OUTPUT: Modified smartCommit in src/utils/git-commit.ts that replaces gitCommit with the plumbing path. Returns commit hash string | null. The CAS-failure path surfaces a recovery recipe.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on smartCommit + a new helper for the recovery-recipe formatting, citing §5.1 edge cases: 'HEAD moved during generation — CAS update-ref fails; MUST NOT force. Surfaces generated message + manual recovery recipe and exits non-zero.'

subtasks.title: Generation-timeout / SIGINT rescue path
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: system_context.md §2.1 — generateCommitMessage is wrapped in a retry() loop. After P1.M2.T2, it will spawn the stagecoach binary. A generation timeout or SIGINT during the plumbing commit flow must never lose the snapshotted work. The TREE_SHA from write-tree (P1.M1.T3.S1) is immutable — it survives any crash.
2. INPUT: TREE_SHA from P1.M1.T3.S1. PARENT_SHA from P1.M1.T3.S1.
3. LOGIC: Add a rescue path in smartCommit: if message generation is interrupted (SIGINT / timeout / process kill) AFTER write-tree succeeded, the function MUST print TREE_SHA + the manual recovery command (`git commit-tree -p <PARENT_SHA> -m "<your message>" <TREE_SHA> | xargs git update-ref HEAD`) to stderr/log so the snapshotted work is recoverable. Register a SIGINT handler (or use try/finally) in the message-generation phase of smartCommit that, if TREE_SHA is set and we haven't committed yet, emits the rescue info. The handler must NOT suppress the signal — it prints the rescue info and re-raises/exits. This ensures no staged work is ever silently lost.
4. OUTPUT: Modified smartCommit with a generation-timeout/SIGINT rescue path. No new exports.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on the rescue path citing §5.1 'Generation timeout / SIGINT: the in-flight generation is killed; the subsystem enters a rescue path that prints TREE_SHA + the manual recovery command so the snapshotted work is never lost.'

subtasks.context_scope:

RESEARCH NOTE: stagecoach-and-agent-factory.md §1.1–§1.4 — stagecoach-ai v0.1.16 exists on npm, downloads a per-platform Go binary at postinstall into ~/.stagecoach/versions/<version>/<goos>-<goarch>/stagecoach. The bin/stagecoach.js shim resolves via STAGECOACH_CACHE_DIR or os.homedir(). The pipeline should resolve the binary similarly. Supported: linux/darwin/windows × amd64/arm64. The package also provides a bin entry (`stagecoach` → `./bin/stagecoach.js`) that could be resolved via require.resolve('stagecoach-ai/bin/stagecoach.js') or by resolving the cache path directly.
2. INPUT: No code inputs — new module + package.json change.

Returns the absolute path string. (c) On missing binary (not installed / postinstall blocked), throw a clear AgentError: 'stagecoach native binary not found at <path>. Run `npm install` to install it (no separate install / PATH needed). See §9.10.1.' — NOT a silent fallback.

tasks.title: Rewrite generateCommitMessage to invoke stagecoach --dry-run --single
tasks.description: Replace the in-process LLM agent call in generateCommitMessage with spawning the stagecoach binary (argv vector, never sh -c). Forward provider/model/style. Capture stdout → descriptive message.

subtasks.title: generateCommitMessage → stagecoach --dry-run --single binary exec
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: stagecoach-and-agent-factory.md §1.3–§1.4 + system_context.md §5.1. CRITICAL: stagecoach reads the REPO INDEX directly — it does NOT accept a diff via stdin. Files MUST be staged in the repo index before invoking stagecoach. Stagecoach snapshots via its own write-tree and generates from that. The message comes via STDOUT. CLI flags: --dry-run (emit message, no commit), --single (one message, no decomposition), --format <auto|plain|conventional|gitmoji>, --provider <pi|claude-code>, --model <resolved>. PRP_COMMIT_STYLE maps: unset→omit --format (native auto), plain→--format plain, conventional→--format conventional, gitmoji→--format gitmoji. Provider/model resolved from §9.2/.hack config.
2. INPUT: resolveStagecoachBinary() from P1.M2.T1.S1. The existing getPrpCommitStyle() from config/constants.ts. Provider/model from the resolved harness config (see src/config/harness.ts, src/config/environment.ts — resolve PRP_AGENT_HARNESS and model). The staged diff is NOT passed as input — stagecoach reads the index.
3. LOGIC: Rewrite generateCommitMessage in src/utils/git-commit.ts: (a) Remove the createCommitMessageAgent + buildCommitMessageSystemPrompt + createPrompt path. (b) Build the argv vector: [stagecoachPath, '--dry-run', '--single']. Append '--format', <style> when PRP_COMMIT_STYLE is explicitly set (not auto/unset). Append '--provider', <resolvedProvider> and '--model', <resolvedModel>. (c) Spawn via child_process.execFile or spawn (argv vector — NEVER sh -c), inheriting env, cwd = repoRoot. (d) Capture stdout → trimmed message. (e) On non-zero exit or empty stdout → throw AgentError (preserving the existing retry/fallback contract in smartCommit — the retry layer wraps this boundary). (f) Remove the gitDiff({staged:true}) call from smartCommit since stagecoach reads the index itself — OR keep it for the fallback path (the fallback placeholder commit doesn't need a diff). The diff variable is no longer needed for generation.
4. OUTPUT: Modified generateCommitMessage(diff?: string) in src/utils/git-commit.ts — the diff parameter may become optional/unused (stagecoach reads the index). The function still returns Promise<string> (the message) and still throws AgentError on failure. The retry/fallback layer in smartCommit is unchanged.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on generateCommitMessage describing binary delegation + --dry-run --single + provider/style forwarding, citing §9.10.1 'The descriptive commit message is generated by delegating to the stagecoach binary.'

subtasks.title: commit-identity-guard test — walk src/ for forbidden identity literals
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: commit-tests-survey.md §6 + system_context.md §5.3. The behavioral fix is already done (formatCommitMessage no longer emits Co-Authored-By). The noreply@anthropic.com string survives only in JSDoc/comments describing the removed bug. There is NO self-source-scan test currently. The guard must walk src/ (and cmd/ if present), skip test files (_test.go/.test.ts/.spec.ts) and the guard's OWN file, skip comment lines (//, /* */, *-prefixed JSDoc), and assert >0 production files visited.
2. INPUT: No code inputs — new test file.
3. LOGIC: Create a new test (e.g. tests/unit/guards/commit-identity-guard.test.ts) that: (a) Recursively walks src/ for .ts files (and cmd/ for .go if present). tasks.title: Bash denylist — pre-exec remote/default-branch-mutation gate
tasks.description: Add a denylist to executeBashCommand in bash-mcp.ts that refuses remote-mutating and default-branch-mutating commands before exec, failing closed on ambiguous matches.

subtasks.title: Implement denylist in executeBashCommand + comprehensive test coverage
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: stagecoach-and-agent-factory.md §2.7 + commit-tests-survey.md §5. bash-mcp.ts (executeBashCommand, line ~118) currently runs ANY command via spawn(command, { shell: true }) with only a timeout guard. ZERO command filtering. The shell: true usage stays (needed for pipes/loops) — the denylist is a pre-exec STRING inspection before spawn. forbidden-operations.test.ts (1107 lines) uses a test-local validateBashCommand helper, NOT production code — new tests must test the actual executeBashCommand.
2. INPUT: The raw command string from BashToolInput.command.
3. LOGIC: In executeBashCommand (src/tools/bash-mcp.ts), BEFORE the spawn call, add a denylist check: inspect the raw command string (case-insensitive). Refuse (return immediately with success:false, non-zero exitCode, clear error message) any command matching: `git push`, `git remote` (any subcommand), `git update-ref`, `git config`, `git reset --hard` (against a shared ref), `git rebase`, `git commit`; `gh repo` (any), `gh api -X PATCH|POST|DELETE`, any `gh api` referencing `default_branch`; `curl`/`wget` to `api.github.com`; any reference to `default_branch`. Ambiguous matches FAIL CLOSED (refuse). Implement as a function isDeniedCommand(command: string): { denied: boolean; reason?: string } that returns before spawn. Legitimate commands (`npx vitest run`, `npm test`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, etc.) MUST still pass. Export isDeniedCommand for testing. Add comprehensive tests covering every denylisted pattern + fail-closed semantics + allowlisted test gates.
4. OUTPUT: New exported function isDeniedCommand() + modified executeBashCommand with pre-exec denylist gate. New/updated tests in tests/unit/tools/bash-mcp.test.ts. Consumed implicitly by all agents using the bash tool (P1.M4.T2).
5. DOCS: JSDoc on executeBashCommand + isDeniedCommand documenting the denylist + fail-closed semantics, citing §9.10.3 'The bash tool MUST refuse — non-zero exit, clear error — any command that matches a repo-remote-mutating or default-branch-mutating operation before exec.'

subtasks.title: Per-persona MCP tool subsets + tests
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: stagecoach-and-agent-factory.md §2.1–§2.5 + §2.8. agent-factory.ts currently exposes a single `MCP_TOOLS = [BASH_MCP, FILESYSTEM_MCP, GIT_MCP]` to ALL personas uniformly. Personas: architect, researcher, coder, qa, cleanup. Each factory function spreads `mcps: MCP_TOOLS` into its config. Factory functions: createArchitectAgent (line ~370), createResearcherAgent (line ~408), createCoderAgent, createQAAgent, createCleanupAgent. GitMCP registers 4 tools: git_status, git_diff, git_add, git_commit. The §9.10.3 matrix maps personas to roles: architect/researcher/coder → 'Research/Planner/Coder' role; qa → 'Validation' role. There is NO 'Commit' persona (commit is internal pipeline code via smartCommit, not an agent). NOTE: cleanup agent is implementation-tier — map it to Coder-equivalent (no bash, read-only git).
2. INPUT: The denylisted BashMCP from P1.M4.T1.S1. The existing GitMCP, FilesystemMCP singletons.
3. LOGIC: (a) Create per-persona tool arrays. Since MCPServer exposes ALL its tools, implement tool subsetting — either: (i) a helper that creates a filtered MCPServer wrapper exposing only allowed tool names, or (ii) construct multiple GitMCP/BashMCP instances with different tool registrations. The simplest approach following existing patterns: create a function buildToolSet(persona: AgentPersona): MCPServer[] that returns: architect/researcher/coder/cleanup → [FilesystemMCP, GitMCP-read-only (git_status + git_diff only)]; qa → [FilesystemMCP, denylisted-BashMCP, full-GitMCP]. No bash for non-qa personas. (b) Replace `mcps: MCP_TOOLS` in each factory function with `mcps: buildToolSet(persona)`. (c) The FilesystemMCP (file_read, file_write, glob_files, grep_search) stays for all personas. (d) Add tests verifying the tool set per persona.
4. OUTPUT: Modified agent-factory.ts with per-persona tool sets + new buildToolSet helper. Updated tests in tests/unit/agents/agent-factory.test.ts. Consumed by all agent factory functions.
5. DOCS: JSDoc on buildToolSet / the tool registration documenting the per-role matrix, citing §9.10.3 'Agent tool access is scoped by role, not granted universally.'
